title: Cutting corners: exciting and magical bounds from the cusp bootstrap
authors: Ryan A. Lanzetta, Ian Moult, Yifan Wang
abstract: An illuminating probe of the dynamics of a line defect is the global geometry of its worldline. For a conformal line defect in a conformal field theory, sharp corners in the worldline, i.e. cusps, host dynamical degrees of freedom characterized in part by a spectrum of scaling dimensions, called cusp anomalous dimensions. We present various general bounds on cusp anomalous dimensions following from unitarity and cutting-and-gluing consistency of different defect geometries. We first establish, for cusps involving conjugate defects, that level crossings upon varying the cusp angle are forbidden between the lightest singlet cusp and any non-singlet cusp, proving that singlet cusps are the lightest. Then, we study line defects arranged in a rectangular geometry, which are subject to bootstrap constraints reminiscent of the spinless modular bootstrap. We find an analytic ``magic" functional that produces an optimal and universal lower bound on the dimension of a right angle bare cusp in terms of the universal defect Casimir energy between the corresponding defect and its conjugate in flat space.
summary: This theoretical paper derives universal, rigorous lower bounds on the anomalous dimensions characterizing sharp corners (cusps) of line defects in a CFT. By applying bootstrap consistency checks across various defect geometries, the authors establish fundamental constraints on the underlying quantum field theory structure. This work provides powerful mathematical tools for constraining physical theories based on symmetry and consistency.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish general, universal bounds on the cusp anomalous dimensions ($\Gamma$) associated with line defects in a Conformal Field Theory (CFT). These bounds are derived from fundamental principles like unitarity and the consistency of defect geometries.
main_result: The authors prove that singlet cusps are the lightest possible cusps and derive an optimal, universal lower bound for the dimension of a right-angle bare cusp using bootstrap constraints.
method: The analysis employs advanced techniques including the Operator State Correspondence (OSC), the Cusp Operator Expansion (COE), and applying bootstrap constraints derived from varying defect geometries (e.g., rectangular or wedge shapes).
model_or_system: The study is set in the context of conformal line defects within a Conformal Field Theory (CFT). The analysis uses concepts from radial and flat quantization to model the dynamics of these defects.
key_observables: Cusp anomalous dimensions ($\Gamma$), the universal defect Casimir energy ($\epsilon_{a ar{a}}$), and the bare cusp dimension ($\Gamma_{a ar{a}}^0(	heta)$).
important_parameters: The cusp angle ($	heta$), the separation distance ($L$), and the geometry of the defect configuration (e.g., right angle, rectangular).
main_assumptions: The theory is assumed to be local, unitary, and possess a complete defect Hilbert space. The derived bounds are claimed to be valid in any scale-invariant theory.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates cusped defect changing operators; Figure 2 shows defect configurations on a sphere punctured at right angles; Figure 3 illustrates the wedge-shaped defect used in the proof of one of the key inequalities.
paper_structure: The paper builds by first establishing foundational results regarding singlet cusps and then deriving increasingly general bounds by applying consistency checks (bootstrap constraints) to increasingly complex defect geometries (e.g., rectangular, cuboid).
why_interesting: While focused on CFT, the techniques involving universal bounds derived from consistency conditions (bootstrap) are highly relevant to understanding critical points and strongly correlated systems where such constraints often appear.
